prompt: During a fast run, Mara breathes faster and more deeply than when she sits still. Which statement best explains why?
choices: Her lungs turn the air she breathes directly into energy for her legs.
Her muscle cells use more oxygen to release energy from sugar.
Her heart pumps air to her leg muscles.
Her working muscles make oxygen, and fast breathing gets rid of the extra.
correct_answer: Her muscle cells use more oxygen to release energy from sugar.
explanation: Working muscle cells release energy from sugar by cellular respiration, which uses oxygen and gives off carbon dioxide. Faster, deeper breathing brings in more oxygen and removes more carbon dioxide.

distractor_rationales.choice: Her lungs turn the air she breathes directly into energy for her legs.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: air itself is energy; lungs only exchange gases, and cells release energy from food.

distractor_rationales.choice: Her heart pumps air to her leg muscles.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: the heart moves air around the body; it pumps blood, which carries dissolved oxygen.

distractor_rationales.choice: Her working muscles make oxygen, and fast breathing gets rid of the extra.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: muscles produce oxygen; they use oxygen and produce carbon dioxide.

real_world_check: Cellular respiration in muscle cells uses oxygen to release energy from glucose, so active muscles raise the body's demand for oxygen and its output of carbon dioxide.

prompt: In one breed of guinea pig, the allele for black fur (B) is dominant over the allele for brown fur (b). Two black guinea pigs that are both Bb have many young together. Which prediction about their young is best?
choices: About one in four of the young will have brown fur.
All of the young will be black.
None of the young can have brown fur, since neither parent is brown.
About half of the young will be brown.
correct_answer: About one in four of the young will have brown fur.
explanation: Each Bb parent passes on B or b with equal chance, so the young are BB, Bb, Bb or bb in a 1:2:1 ratio. Only bb young are brown, which is about one out of every four.

distractor_rationales.choice: All of the young will be black.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: a dominant allele shows up in every offspring; bb young can still occur and be brown.

distractor_rationales.choice: None of the young can have brown fur, since neither parent is brown.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: young can show only traits their parents show; hidden recessive alleles can pair up.

distractor_rationales.choice: About half of the young will be brown.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: carrying one b allele gives a one-in-two chance of brown; a young needs b from both parents.

real_world_check: A cross between two heterozygous parents (Bb x Bb) is expected to give about 25 percent offspring showing the recessive trait.
